units.translation: ⟦1⟧ of the Erinyes only here. The difficult next sentence is at least less unclear at its end. ⟦2⟧〈⟦3⟧〉 ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧ gives the sense that one should be consoled by the (even worse) fate of another, though in vain. ⟦6⟧ in the sense of abating (opposite ⟦7⟧) is not demonstrable, even if late authors like Philostratus and Dio Cassius use ⟦8⟧ in this way, and in the sense of "yielding" (opposite ⟦9⟧) Aristotle also has it (Π. ⟦10⟧. ⟦11⟧. 698 b 15); the scholiast explains ⟦12⟧, which leads to ⟦13⟧ (Paley): ⟦14⟧ ⟦15⟧. However, ⟦16⟧ (g, and so Herm.) lies closer and is supported by Homer v 53 ⟦17⟧; moreover, ⟦18⟧ means to take upon oneself, which comes close to ⟦19⟧. In the last colon either ⟦20⟧ or ⟦21⟧ must be removed; ⟦22⟧ now echoes ⟦23⟧ of the strophe, and Hermann supports ⟦24⟧ with ⟦25⟧: ⟦26⟧, ⟦27⟧. Of the scholiasts, one accepts ⟦28⟧, the other does not: ⟦29⟧, so si dis placet not only ⟦30⟧ "criminal", but also active for passive. ⟦31⟧, which lies closer to the transmitted text than ⟦32⟧, requires after it ⟦33⟧ instead of ⟦34⟧ (⟦35⟧ 〈⟦36⟧〉 Hartung, with a different rhythm, which he also restored in the strophe). But in the first words of the sentence ⟦37⟧ contends with ⟦38⟧, and if this is to be connected with ⟦39⟧, then ⟦40⟧ is without an object, and vice versa. The simplest solution is probably to emend ⟦41⟧ to ⟦42⟧ (sua): each tells his misfortune and inquires about that of his neighbor, or rather learns of it, since one tries to console him with it. ⟦43⟧ in the sense of suus already at 367.
a cessation and remission of toils
but some wretched man consoles in vain
but you will slip under evils
why do you console me in my grief?
each of the murderers will be consoled

⟦1⟧: (Kühner-Blass I, 185) is the spelling of the second Delphic Hymn (V. 20), Weil Études de littérat. et de rythmique gr. p. 71. ⟦2⟧ otherwise active, ⟦3⟧ etc.; but ⟦4⟧ Hik. 111 etc. The insertion of ⟦5⟧ after ⟦6⟧ (but goddess here, not ⟦7⟧) seems unnecessary, since also Str. 3, 3 is an independent dipody; nor even fitting in the pathetic invocation.
513 ⟦1⟧ is according to Wecklein (cf. on 450); to me the ⟦2⟧ of the antistrophe seems quite unreliable because of the sense, cf. there.
